Everything below comes from the census cache, from G3's integer V3 replay (imported read-only) and from the census's cached full blocks, which also contain reverted transactions. Some risks are outside this lens and stay open: whether the operator reacts to our buy (not measurable, only 2 stranger buys), whether $0.02 gas covers a V3 round trip including the approve (no receipts in the cache), and whether the +2 landing measured on v4 holds on V3.
reasons:
The rule can be executed as described once the V3 path exists, and the token can be sold.
1) Recognising the launch from the feed. I read 3 real inputs (x01). All 111 are selector d27d1e00, 356 B, value 0, type 2, priority 1, to a different contract each time, all with code hash 89885b75 and size 5050. The calldata has 11 words: word 0 is the token; words 1, 3 and 7 are one address (39 values), the "collector". That collector deployed the token 4-6 blocks before the launch (7 of 7 deploys found in the cached blocks) and made all 63 first pulls. Words 9-10 are empty bytes; word 6 is a 0/1 flag. The pool address is CREATE2(factory, token, WETH, fee 100) with the canonical V3 init code hash: it matches in 111 of 111. The launcher is CREATE(launch wallet, nonce-1) in 111 of 111. It is deployed 7-13 blocks before the launch with the same 5093-byte initcode (7 of 7 cached), and its runtime hashes to 89885b75. So the code-hash key can be checked from the feed (by seeing the earlier CREATE) or with one eth_getCode, with 6 s to spare before +60. Selector + 356 B + value 0 is unique: it appears on 111 of 111 census launches, and the 9 other 356-B launches carry 0.1 ETH. In 156,461 cached whole blocks every d27d1e00 tx (18) is a census launch.
2) The entry offset is K=60, so there is no race. Before +60 the pools have p90 3 swaps and at most 0.0055 ETH of buys; 2 pools have a swap in block +60. Buy blocks +58 to +64 give the same result. Selling at +258 to +264 gives $750-787/day. With a one-block slip on both sides the result is +114.9% and $784/day (x05).
3) The buys we sell into carry ETH value. In the [+60, +260) windows, 34.83 of 34.99 ETH comes through SwapRouter02 0xcaf681a6. Of the fetched exactInputSingle buys, 167 have msg.value = amountIn (19.47 ETH) and 29 are value-0 (0.01 ETH in total). The 131 unfetched Router02 buys (15.34 ETH) go to single-use recipients. In the full blocks, 158 of 160 buy attempts carry value. The feed can price these buys, although the fixed +260 exit does not need it.
4) The token. I cut the runtime out of 7 deploy initcodes (both templates). Their skeleton hash matches the pools, and the masked hash is the same within each template (100 tokens and 11). Both are plain OpenZeppelin v5 ERC20: the 9 standard functions (97c7ba1b adds one string getter on slot 5) and only the OZ ERC20 errors. There is no CALL, ORIGIN, TIMESTAMP or NUMBER and no owner. Storage is only balances, allowances, supply and strings. So there is no tax, blacklist, whitelist or trading switch.
Behaviour agrees. Of 83 wallets that both bought and sold, 56 sold exactly what they bought (ratio 1.000). Wallets seen in at least 3 pools sold successfully 56 times (20 wallets, 44 pools). In the full blocks, 155 of 157 router multicall sells (exactInputSingle + unwrapWETH9) succeeded. The 2 failures had a non-zero min-out and came from a wallet whose other sells succeeded.
5) Operator min-out. If the fleet's quotes were taken before our buy, our 0.0058 buy (a 1.16% price move) would push 3-4 of the 158 readable non-zero min-outs in the window into a revert. Dropping those buys gives $775/day. Since the first fleet buy comes at +111 or later, quotes are more likely taken after our buy.
6) Depth. In 88 of 111 pools the pool holds less than 0.01 ETH at +260, so our sell mostly gets our own ETH back. At larger stakes the trips grow: 19 at 0.05 ETH and 28 at 0.1 ETH.
